title: PGYTECH RetroVa Gives the iPhone a 400mm Reach and a Real Camera Feel
summary: PGYTECH launches RetroVa telephoto accessory giving iPhones a 400mm reach
detailed: PGYTECH expanded its RetroVa kit lineup to support iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max and 18 Pro/Pro Max series with new 2X and 4X telephoto lens options.

The hardware kit features a camera-style Bluetooth grip weighing 63 to 65.4 grams, a polycarbonate MagSafe case, focal range equivalents up to 400mm, and a built-in microSD slot supporting UHS-I and UHS-II cards for RAW photos and 4K video up to 120fps.
The physical grip includes a shutter button with half-press focus, a zoom lever, a control dial for exposure, ISO, white balance, or shutter speed, and a multi-function power and pairing button.
The product matters because it bridges the gap between smartphones and dedicated cameras by providing physical camera controls and optical clarity at extended focal ranges.
sentences: PGYTECH is best known for camera bags, tripods and straps, and in the phone world for telephoto extender lenses designed for Vivo and Oppo flagships.
Its RetroVa kit brings that lens work to the iPhone.

The system first appeared on Kickstarter in January 2026 for the iPhone 16 Pro and 17 Pro families, combining a camera-style Bluetooth grip, retro-style case, and a 2.35x teleconverter for the phone’s telephoto lens.
The newest version designed for the iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max and 18 Pro/Pro Max series brings in a lighter and smaller 2X lens, along with a 4X telephoto lens as an alternative.
This all provides focal range that simply doesn’t work as well when using the phone itself.
With 200mm, 235mm, and 400mm equivalents, the iPhone can reach farther with more optical clarity.
A dedicated app also offers old school film simulations and manual controls for composition to let you decide how you want your images to look.

The RetroVa All-in-One Ultimate Gift Set comes in Graphite Black, while the 4X lens, grip, and the case are also sold separately and in smaller bundles, offering users different ways to put the kit together.

RetroVa Black Friday deal: From November 19 to 30, the RetroVa All-in-One Ultimate Gift Set (Graphite Black, iPhone 17/18 Pro Max) is 10% off, and PetaPixel readers can take an extra 10% off with code BYTEDDYK.
Buy it on Amazon or directly from PGYTECH.

The Ultimate Gift Set brings them all together in the box: the 4X telephoto lens, a lens adapter bracket, lens pouch, RetroVa phone case, grip, a photography strap, and an Arca-Swiss compatible tripod collar for the lens.
The case is polycarbonate and works with MagSafe, leaving the proverbial door open for additional magnetic accessories.
Though it has a lip over the edges, you can still use the case with a screen protector on the phone itself.
The lightweight grip weighs 63 grams for the Pro and 65.4 grams for the Pro Max.
It carries physical controls, a built-in microSD slot, and a standard 1/4-inch socket on the base for tripods and monopods.
It slides into the phone’s USB-C port with a lock switch that holds it firmly in place, though it actually pairs and connects to the device via Bluetooth.
It’s important to get the right size because there are separate variants for the Pro and Pro Max.
While the lens mount is the same on either build, you can’t slide a Pro grip into the Pro Max, for instance.
That also goes for the case, which is the most integral piece because that’s what everything else in the kit attaches to.
Fortunately, since the iPhone 17 Pro and 18 Pro models share the same dimensions, you don’t need to worry about compatibility in that regard.
The shutter button functions a lot like a typical camera would: half-press to focus, press to take the shot, or hold it down for a burst.
The zoom lever right under it can either skip between focal lengths in Vintage mode or adjust zoom more freely in the Standard setting.
Below that is the control dial that you can choose to adjust exposure, ISO, white balance, or shutter speed.
Lastly, the multi-function button acts as power on/off, switches modes, and sets up Bluetooth pairing.
A small LED next to it indicates pairing and a solid connection.
The microSD card slot (UHS-I or UHS-II) underneath is another handy way to save excess photos or video, albeit with some key parameters.
You can readily save RAW photos or 4K video to it, only you’re limited to HEVC-coded footage and max 120fps.
Plug the grip into a laptop where you can then offload the content directly.
If you record in Apple’s Camera app, video automatically goes to the card when you use supported formats, while PGYTECH’s app supports more recording formats.
Even third-party apps that can record to external storage can recognize the card, too.
PGYTECH also makes 62mm and 67mm filter adapter rings sold separately from the available kits.
They’re not included in any of them, though will work just fine with any filters in those two respective sizes.
Being a separate piece, you just slide out the lens adapter ring and bring in the filter adapter instead.
There is no way to use a filter with the teleconverter lenses themselves, since the filter adapter covers the iPhone’s entire rear array.
PGYTECH designed the kit to work with a dedicated companion app called PGYTECH: Pro Camera & Editor.
It’s free to download, only requiring iOS 17 or later to run.
You do, however, need to be diligent about keeping it up to date because if you don’t, the app may lock you out of all the manual control settings.
A pop-up notice stating that a subscription is required to unlock those pro features isn’t actually necessary.
Update the app and that message disappears.

While there is an Auto mode available, Manual provides controls for exposure, shutter speed, ISO, white balance, tint, and filters, which you can then map to the grip by going to Settings->Hardware Settings.
You will need to ensure the grip is on and once connected via Bluetooth, select RetroVa in the drop-down menu to pick what you want.
At any point within that section, you can always look at tutorials on connecting the grip and a video FAQ as well.
Unless you explicitly make your own manual adjustments, the app’s camera interface treats everything as if it was in Auto.
So, shutter speed, ISO, white balance, and tint will all dynamically shift based on what’s in frame.
Tap to focus works just like any other camera app would.

One difference, though, is if you have Focus Assist on (focus peaking by another name), you will see where the camera is actually focusing after you tap, giving you an indication of where the focal plane is.
Other manual controls, like a histogram and priority facial recognition (the camera will always focus on a face first in this setting), are elective.
Standard bits, like a timer, live photo, watermark, and aspect ratio (1:1, 4:3, and 16:9) round out much of what’s left.
There is a Dive Mode that switches controls to physical buttons for underwater photos and video, while also applying an “underwater filter” as a copy of the original when captured.
You can make separate manual settings adjustments for this mode, too.

In addition to about 15 standard filters, PGYTECH offers a series of nostalgic film simulations, ranging from Classic Negative and Nostalgic Negative to Kodak Gold 200, Fujifilm PRO Neg Std, Velvia 100, Classic Chrome, FujiColor C200, Tungsten 500, and Bleach Bypass.
Choose any one at any time and adjust the intensity from 0-100.
These simulations apply no matter what image format you shoot with and aren’t limited to still photos: they work with video, too.

The app includes a Retro Film mode that features the same set of film simulations, except it changes the hybrid zoom ranges to include 35mm and 50mm equivalents to better match traditional prime lenses.
Otherwise, images process the same way as the Photo mode.
It’s also possible to apply any of these filters on a photo after you capture it within the in-app editing suite, including HSL for some color grading.
Beauty features also present a variety of options for those seeking that kind of detail.
Under Creative, there are templates for sharing or social media.
An on-device AI tool in the Adjust section lets you try enhancing detail in images by either using HD to improve clarity or AI HD to restore detail in softer images.
You need to download it to make it work on-device rather than in the cloud but once it’s there, you can utilize it any time.
